Maya: Quick sync — proposing we carve out the 'Adaptive Prefetch' initiative into two phases so runtime/infra/security can sign off. Phase 1 = warm routing + KV caching (no customer secrets). Phase 2 = tenant-level prefetch + private pilot (KMS/HSM + audit). Need alignment on acceptance, sizing, rollout owners, and blockers. cc @Jordan @Priya @Ken
Jordan: Quick q — for phase1 what's the p95 target we should design against? 200ms for cold misses seems optimistic. Also we need a fallback model variant if cache misses spike.
Priya: For sizing, how many concurrent prewarm shards are we expecting? If phase1 uses shared GPU pool, plan for ~20% burst capacity. I need a traffic shape to get exact numbers.
Ken: For phase2 private pilot we will require KMS integration + audit logs + network egress rules. Can we keep phase1 strictly no-customer-data so security review is lighter? :thinking_face:
Maya: Yes — phase1 explicitly no customer secrets, only inference-level prefixes for public demos. Phase2 will be the only one touching tenant secrets. I'll update the spec to call this out.
Jordan: Runtime asks: default KV TTL = 10m (can tune). Need canary toggles per-tenant + a simple fallback to model-variant B when latency > threshold. Also will add a perf regression test. Example quick hit: `curl -X POST /prefetch -d '{"key":"abc"}'` to simulate.
Priya: Toggle + canary sounds good. Also we prefer deployments in low-traffic weekday mornings. Who owns rollback playbook? infra or eng oncall?
Maya: Product will own rollout plan (who/when), eng (Jordan + runtime) will own rollback runbook and test cases. Infra (Priya) owns capacity reservations and deployment windows. Security (Ken) owns the phase-gated checklist for phase2.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Meeting created: "Adaptive Prefetch Carveout triage" Mon 10:00 — invites: Maya, Jordan, Priya, Ken, Alex
Jordan: I'll draft the runtime runbook + a perf test harness by Friday and bring a short demo to the triage.
Priya: If you can post the expected QPS shape by EOD I'll start preliminary sizing and a capacity delta table.
Ken: I'll draft the security checklist for phase2 (KMS, audit logs, HSM ops, private subnet rules) and flag any compliance redlines by next Wed.
Alex: One note — product should define 'acceptance' for phase1: e.g., no perf regressions >5% and feature toggles working per-tenant with <1% error rate. That will help QA signoff.
Maya: Great callouts. Action items recap: Jordan -> runtime runbook + perf tests (Fri). Priya -> capacity numbers + deployment windows (Tue). Ken -> security checklist for phase2 (next Wed). Maya -> update spec and add acceptance criteria to docs, schedule Monday triage 10am.
Jordan: I'll also include a quick script to simulate cache stampede and validate fallback behavior.
Priya: :thumbsup: if we get traffic shape I'll post a sizing table before the meeting.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll post the updated spec in #docs and ping here when it's live. If anyone can't make Mon 10 please suggest an alternative slot.
